$comment: Every place a string can appear. A translator reading a string alone cannot tell a button from a sentence, or a title from a warning; this says which surface it is on and what a reader is doing when they see it.

welcome.name: Welcome / permission screen
welcome.shown: The first thing a new reader sees, and again whenever Full Disk Access is missing. Also shown when drives set to reopen after a restart could not be opened because the permission has gone.
welcome.purpose: Explain that macOS will not let any app read a raw disk without Full Disk Access, and walk through granting it in three numbered steps.
welcome.tone: Plain and unhurried. Nothing has gone wrong; something has to be switched on.
welcome.notes: Carries a screenshot of the macOS Full Disk Access pane. Step 1 names a System Settings pane: use Apple's own wording for that pane in this language, or leave it in English where macOS is not offered in this language. See terms.json.

drive-list.name: Drive list
drive-list.shown: After scanning, whenever there is at least one drive or disk image to show.
drive-list.purpose: List what can be opened. Each row carries a name, a size, how it is connected, and what the volume may be.
drive-list.tone: Neutral labels. Rows are read at a glance, so short.
drive-list.notes: The subtitle under a row is assembled from untranslated technical parts (size, USB, BitLocker/NTFS, disk4s1) joined by a middle dot. It is not translated.

unlock.name: Unlock screen
unlock.shown: After choosing a drive or opening a disk image, before it is opened.
unlock.purpose: Take the passphrase or recovery key, say what is known about the drive, and offer to open it writable or read-only.
unlock.tone: Direct. This is where somebody types a secret.
unlock.notes: Holds the blue note for a drive that turns out not to be encrypted, the note about what may be written to an image format, and the panel of outstanding macOS permissions.

working.name: Opening screen
working.shown: While a drive is being unlocked and mounted, which takes several seconds.
working.purpose: Show which step the mount has reached so that a wait does not look like a hang.
working.notes: The step names are also shown on the failure screen, where one of them is marked as the step it stopped at.

mounted.name: Opened screen
mounted.shown: Once a drive is open and visible in Finder.
mounted.purpose: Confirm it worked, say where it is, and offer to show it in Finder.
mounted.notes: Names Finder and its sidebar. Finder is a product name; see terms.json.

failure.name: Failure screen
failure.shown: When a drive could not be opened.
failure.purpose: Say what went wrong in one sentence, mark which step it stopped at, and offer to try again or report it.
failure.tone: Factual, never apologetic, never alarming. Most failures are a mistyped passphrase.
failure.notes: The one-sentence summary is chosen by matching the engine's own output; those sentences live in diagnosis.*

open-image.name: Opening a disk image
open-image.shown: After File → Open Disk Image, while a file is examined, and if it cannot be opened.
open-image.purpose: Report progress, report that macOS opened the image itself, or say why the file cannot be opened.
open-image.notes: The failure title is the same for every reason; the sentence under it is the particular reason.

open-drive.name: Open Drive sheet
open-drive.purpose: List every disk on the Mac, including the ones this app will not touch, and say why each is or is not offered.
open-drive.tone: A table. Labels rather than sentences.
open-drive.notes: Rows for the system disk and for disks macOS reads itself are shown but not offered.

settings.name: Settings
settings.shown: From the menu bar or the gear in the header.
settings.purpose: Appearance, language, the menu bar icon, saved passphrases, updates.
settings.tone: Standard macOS settings labels: short, capitalised as a title.
settings.notes: The language picker lists languages in their own language, which macOS supplies; those names are never translated here.

help.name: Help sheet
help.shown: From the question mark in the header.
help.purpose: Explain what the app does, what it can open, how it works, what it costs in privacy, and the licence.
help.tone: The longest prose in the app. Explanatory, complete sentences, no marketing.
help.notes: Contains the GPL notice, which is not translated, and format names, which are not translated.

report.name: Report an Issue sheet
report.shown: From the ladybird in the header, or from the failure screen.
report.purpose: Collect a description, show exactly what will be sent, and offer to copy it or open an issue.
report.tone: Reassuring about what is and is not included. Nothing is sent without being shown first.
report.notes: The report body itself is English and is not translated: it is read by whoever fixes the fault.

uninstall.name: Uninstall sheet
uninstall.purpose: Say what removing the app takes with it, and ask about saved passphrases separately.
uninstall.tone: Careful. This is destructive and irreversible.

menus.name: Menu bar and app menus
menus.shown: Always, plus a status icon while a drive is open.
menus.purpose: File, Window and Help menu items, the eject items in the status menu, and the alerts they raise.
menus.tone: macOS menu conventions: title case in English, an ellipsis where a dialogue follows.

diagnosis.name: Failure sentences
diagnosis.kind: text, shown on the failure screen
diagnosis.shown: One is chosen when a mount fails, by matching the engine's output.
diagnosis.purpose: Turn a technical failure into one sentence a reader can act on.
diagnosis.tone: Say what happened and what to do. Never blame the reader, never print an error code.
diagnosis.notes: Each carries a rule name in the code. Several mention Windows, hibernation or a filesystem name.

formats.name: Disk image refusals
formats.kind: text, shown in the Opening a disk image sheet
formats.shown: When a file cannot be opened, one sentence says why.
formats.purpose: Name the format and say what would work instead.
formats.tone: Technical but not cryptic. Format names are never translated.
formats.notes: VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, qcow2 and raw image are product formats; see terms.json.

notices.name: Notices and announcements
notices.shown: Above a list or under a title, when something happened that is worth one sentence.
notices.purpose: A drive that went away, a permission that was refused, a count of volumes.

first-launch.name: Early development notice
first-launch.shown: Once, on the first launch of a given build, as soon as the drive list is up. It waits for permission to have been given and the scan to have finished, so it never appears beside another sheet.
first-launch.purpose: Say that the app is early, that reading a drive and copying off it is the safe use, and that writing should be treated as experimental.
first-launch.tone: Plain and calm. It is not a warning dialog and there is nothing to decide; the only button says OK.
first-launch.notes: The app's own name appears twice as a placeholder, because an unbranded build carries a different name.
